messages:
anya: quick update from the tidepool13b quant smoke run — finished int6 and int8 slices + some longform evals. sharing econ + quality notes below

devin: nice. top-line?

anya: int6 wins ~38–42% token-cost reduction vs int8 on our GPU profiles (varies with seq len). throughput up ~1.6x.

samir: what about quality? any regressions we care about for GTN slices?

anya: on short Q/A prompts, human-anchored accuracy ~flat (within noise). on the summarize_long slice we see ~1.1–1.4% absolute drop in recall/ROUGE-L depending on prompt priming. biggest hits on very long context >2k tokens.

lina: can you quantify per-1M-token cost numbers? product wants a simple dropdown for guidance.

anya: rough ballpark on our infra: int8 path ~ $48 / 1M tokens; int6 path ~ $29 / 1M tokens (these include batching improvements and cache win assumptions).

devin: oof, that delta is material. does latency change? tail percentiles?

anya: p50 ~ same, p95 down ~10–15% (because faster kernels). p99 similar but depends on KV cache misses; long sequences spike p99 on int6 sometimes due to memory compaction GC on the runtime (we traced a couple).

samir: GC? need an infra note + workaround for p99. Lina, is product okay with gap on long-form?

lina: product care: for chat completions GTN wants cost-savings but not at expense of hallucination/ factual drop. 1.3% recall drop on longform might be acceptable if we can auto-route problematic prompts. 

anya: recommended routing strategy: default -> int6 for all traffic except: 1) prompts with expected >1024 tokens output 2) eval signals from prompt classifier that detect longform tasks 3) health-check slices that trip recall threshold --> route to int8. Also keep a tiny % (0.5%) canary to int8 for drift detection.

devin: ops questions: what flag toggles the routing policy? can we set fallback quickly?

samir: infra-bot ran a canary deploy earlier today: infra-bot: deploy tidepool13b-int6-canary -> success (3 nodes, us-west2) :thumbsup:

infra-bot: logs: avg QPS 220, mean latency 110ms, p95 260ms, p99 410ms during the smoke.

anya: for rollout plan: start with 10% traffic -> monitor recall on GTN slices + latency tails for 24h -> expand to 50% if no regression -> 100% but keep canary + fallback. Add automatic fallback when recall on any monitored eval drops >0.8% absolute over baseline.

lina: product asks: can we present a simple guidance card in Console: "Int6: ~40% cheaper, recommended for default; Int8: higher fidelity for long-form/critical outputs." Also show estimated monthly savings based on current usage.

devin: engineering asks: do we need model changes (prompt tuning) to recover the 1.2%?

anya: short-term: prompt tweaks (system priming and sample weighting) buy back ~0.4–0.6%. medium-term: small calibration head or distillation pass might recover more but is longer.

samir: infra mitigations for p99: add a small memory pressure threshold that forces ephemeral KV flush for excessively long sequences; we can also route those to int8 automatically.

lina: action items: 1) ops -> samir to enable routing flag + canary (today) 2) ml -> anya to push a prompt-tweak PR and a 0.5% canary probe for drift (tomorrow) 3) product -> lina to draft Console guidance card and savings calc (EOD)

anya: adding eval note: attach the longform sample that triggered the worst-case regression to the ticket (we should include prompt+gold).

samir: doing the routing flag now, will post the flag name and rollout command once live.

devin: thanks all — this feels like a pragmatic win. keep the fallback thresholds conservative and let's not roll past 50% without the recall hooks green. :thumbsup:
